title: Daily Noocracy Report — AI Infrastructure Is Becoming an Electricity Story
caption:
DAILY NOOCRACY REPORT — SEPTEMBER 24, 2026

AI infrastructure is increasingly constrained by power, grid capacity, and financing—not just chips.

The International Energy Agency projects global data-centre electricity use to rise from about 485 TWh in 2025 to roughly 950 TWh in 2030, while electricity consumption from AI-focused data centres grows even faster. That means the economics of AI increasingly depend on generation capacity, transmission, interconnection queues, cooling, and capital discipline.

At the same time, bond investors are becoming more selective about the large volume of debt needed to fund AI infrastructure. The signal is straightforward: compute demand may keep rising, but infrastructure returns still have to justify the capital required to build and power it.

NOOCRATIC VIEW:
• Compute needs electricity.
• Electricity needs infrastructure.
• Infrastructure needs disciplined capital.
• Scale without efficiency becomes fragility.

WATCH NEXT:
Power contracts, interconnection delays, utilization rates, financing costs, and whether AI efficiency gains offset higher usage.
